question: A project's instructions say "write for our executive committee". The same project is also used to produce customer-facing FAQ answers. What is the greatest risk here?
options: A) The project can no longer hold uploaded documents, because an audience rule takes the place of the knowledge base.
B) Customer material inherits an executive register that is wrong for its readers, and the mismatch is easy to miss.
C) Every FAQ answer is saved as a separate project, since a second audience needs its own workspace to exist.
D) The instruction blocks any request that is not addressed to the executive committee, so the FAQ chats fail.
correct_answers: B) Customer material inherits an executive register that is wrong for its readers, and the mismatch is easy to miss.
explanations: Audience direction and uploaded knowledge are independent and coexist without issue.
Correct. One durable audience rule silently mis-shapes every piece of work aimed at a different audience.
Nothing creates projects automatically; the workspace is unchanged by what is asked in it.
An audience instruction shapes style; it does not reject requests.
